key_insight: ENFR makes Bayesian model evidence easier to estimate by learning an amortized, simulation-based surrogate that can be reused across many inference tasks. It turns a traditionally expensive quantity into a practical tool for model comparison, misspecification testing, and goodness-of-fit assessment.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of computing model evidence, \(\mathcal{Z} = p(x \mid \mathcal{M})\), which is often intractable even when the likelihood is available. This limits reliable Bayesian model selection and diagnostic testing in both likelihood-based and simulation-based settings.
method: Builds Evidence Networks that learn to estimate model evidence directly from data.
Uses flow-matched references to support amortized inference, enabling efficient reuse across datasets or simulations.
Targets simulation-based model inference, where exact likelihoods are unavailable or expensive to evaluate.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more practical way to compare models and detect misspecification without relying on fragile hand-crafted discrepancy statistics. It can improve reliability in scientific ML, Bayesian workflows, and simulation-based inference pipelines.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing data \u2192 Evidence Network \u2192 estimated evidence \u2192 model selection/testing
A side-by-side comparison of standard discrepancy metrics vs. evidence-based inference
An icon-based illustration of simulation, flow matching, and amortization
A bar chart or scorecard showing evidence estimates across candidate models
paper_title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
paper_authors: Kai Lehman, Jameson Dong, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro, Niall Jeffrey, Benjamin D. Wandelt
